item.title: Governo federal assina aporte de R$3 bi em ponte Salvador-Ilha de Itaparica
item.description: O Ministério dos Transportes anunciou nesta terça-feira assinatura de termo para aporte de R$3 bilhões no projeto de construção da segunda maior ponte do Brasil, a ponte Salvador-Ilha de Itaparica, na Bahia, com 12,4 quilômetros de extensão.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O Ministério dos Transportes anunciou nesta terça-feira assinatura de termo para aporte de R$3 bilhões no projeto de construção da segunda maior ponte do Brasil, a ponte Salvador-Ilha de Itaparica, na Bahia, com 12,4 quilômetros de extensão. O projeto será a maior ponte da América Latina sobre lâmina d’água e integra uma parceria público-privada (PPP) entre o governo da Bahia e um consórcio de empresas chinesas. O empreendimento foi incluído no Novo Programa de Aceleração do Crescimento (PAC). A travessia, que hoje leva cerca de uma hora, deverá ser feita em 15 minutos, podendo reduzir em até 200 quilômetros o percurso de cargas, afirmou o ministério. A previsão para conclusão dos trabalhos é meados de 2031, segundo o governo baiano. A PPP da ponte foi arrematada em 2019 por um consórcio de três empresas chinesas: China Communications Construction (601800.SS) , CCCC South America Regional Company e China Railway 20 Bureau Group Corporation, uma unidade da China Railway Construction Corp (601186.SS) .

item.title: Iran shifting tactics to step up attacks on shipping before US vote, officials say
item.description: Iran is deploying new tactics to target ships sailing through the Strait of Hormuz as it seeks to keep oil prices high and influence the US midterm elections, two senior Iranian officials told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Parisa Hafezi, Jonathan Saul, Phil Stewart
item.content:encoded: Iran is deploying new tactics to target ships sailing through the Strait of Hormuz as it seeks to keep oil prices high and influence the US midterm elections, two senior Iranian officials told Reuters. Tehran has tried to exert control over the Strait of Hormuz since the US and Israel launched strikes against Iran on February 28. It has restricted passage through the waterway, which carried about a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas trade before the war , in an effort to gain leverage over Washington. Its threats and attacks have severely curtailed traffic through the strait, driving up [USN:L1N45Z00X TEXT:"oil prices"], though some oil has [USN:L6N42O131 TEXT:"continued to transit"]. The two officials declined to provide details of the new strategy, but one said that Iran had started using different offensive tactics against vessels it considered in violation of its restrictions about 10 days ago, adding that this had led to an increase in attacks on such ships. The strategy included a change in the type as well as the pace of attacks, with one goal being to influence the outcome of the US vote, they said. "The aim is to frustrate efforts by the United States and its allies to bring down global oil prices," one of the two officials said. The decision to adopt the new strategy had been taken at the highest levels of Iran’s leadership and was fully coordinated across the country’s ruling system, the officials said. IRAN USING SPOTTERS A US military official, speaking on condition of anonymity, confirmed that Iran had changed tactics in one significant way: after the US destroyed much of Iran’s radar capabilities, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) had started using unarmed spotters in small boats to identify potential targets, including US naval vessels, the official said. Last week, in a previously unreported incident, the US military determined that Iranian spotters were operating from a dhow, calling in targets to the IRGC, the official said. US forces confronted the vessel, told its occupants to abandon ship and then destroyed it. There were no casualties, the US official said. Unwilling to risk its remaining fast boats, Iran had been unable to prevent a ramp-up in oil exports through the strait, the official said, particularly after US strikes devastated its navy. The war — and its [USN:L6N4530XO TEXT:"$3 billion monthly price tag"] — has become a key issue on the US campaign trail for November's midterm elections , which will decide control of Congress. US President Donald Trump has been [USN:L1N45T10U TEXT:"weighing next steps"] against Iran, but has said he [USN:L1N45U0PH TEXT:"will not attack"] again before the vote. The US has meanwhile been pressing its own naval blockade of Iranian ports and [USN:L1N45U0QQ TEXT:"extending sanctions"] as it tries to pile [USN:L6N45K0UX TEXT:"economic pressure"] on Tehran to reach a deal to end the conflict. The standoff over Hormuz has left global energy markets exposed to further disruption, with the threat of attacks and high shipping and insurance costs complicating efforts to restore normal traffic. In recent days, attacks on commercial ships still sailing through the strait have [USN:L1N45T0HL TEXT:"surged to their highest level"] since the war began, according to independent data. There have been at least five incidents in the past 48 hours involving tankers and other commercial ships around the Hormuz area, including drone strikes, according to data analysis from maritime security sources and incidents reported to British navy-affiliated agency United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO). That approximately mirrored the rate of attacks on October 3-5, pointing to a new escalation, according to data from the UN shipping agency, the International Maritime Organization. "There is a tempo increase in strikes, which looks deliberate," one maritime security source said. ATTACKS OVER AN EXPANDED AREA As part of the new strategy, Tehran will also expand the geographical scope of its operations beyond the Strait of Hormuz to the Gulf of Oman and waters further afield, the officials said. Analysis by maritime security sources based on attacks reported to UKMTO and maritime security companies in the region suggest this may already be happening. They show Iran targeting ships in areas beyond the Strait of Hormuz, including waters off the coast of Qatar and the United Arab Emirates, in recent days. The second Iranian official added that Tehran would not allow Trump to bring down oil prices before the November elections. "Just when they think they are getting close to the point where prices will fall, we will push them away from it. This is a game of chess,” the second official said. "Such vessels would be safe nowhere, even outside the Strait of Hormuz." The Pentagon and Iran's Foreign Ministry did not immediately respond to requests for comment. COMPLETE CLOSURE OF HORMUZ SOON, SAYS IRANIAN OFFICIAL Both Iranian officials said Tehran is moving towards a situation in which no vessel violating its restrictions would be able to pass through the strait. "It will be complete closure soon," one of the officials said. In its latest report on Sunday, the US Navy-led Joint Maritime Information Center (JMIC) said the threat to merchant shipping in the Strait of Hormuz remained "severe", the second-highest level. "IRGC attacks, attempted attacks, and/or harassment activity persisted including UAV overflight, targeted surveillance of merchant shipping, and occasional VHF hailing," JMIC said.

item.title: Ukrainian ex-officer stands trial in Germany over Nord Stream bombing
item.description: A Ukrainian ex-military officer goes on trial in Germany on Wednesday, accused of organising the secret operation that blew up the Nord Stream gas pipelines in September 2022, severing western Europe from the biggest source of Russian natural gas.
item.dc:creator: Miranda Murray
item.content:encoded: A Ukrainian ex-military officer goes on trial in Germany on Wednesday, accused of organising the secret operation that blew up the Nord Stream gas pipelines in September 2022, severing western Europe from the biggest source of Russian natural gas. The suspect, identified under German privacy rules only as Serhii K., is accused of leading a group of Ukrainian agents including divers and an explosives expert to mount one of the biggest infrastructure sabotage operations of modern times. The case will provide the first opportunity for a public hearing of evidence gathered during a years-long investigation, which has been diplomatically and politically awkward for a German government that remains staunchly supportive of Ukraine despite the investigative trail linking Kyiv to the crime. Prosecutors have alleged that Serhii K., who was arrested under an international warrant in Italy last year, worked with other members of the military to plan the [USN:L8N3UD0YM TEXT:"clandestine operation"] on behalf of unidentified Ukrainian state entities. Serhii K. has denied any involvement in the blasts that ruptured the 1,200-km (750-mile)-long Baltic Sea pipeline. The government in Kyiv has also denied any involvement, a sensitive point in its relations with Germany, Ukraine's largest European supplier of military aid. The Russian government said on Monday it expected a "just verdict" that would reveal the names of the perpetrators and those who ordered the operation. German prosecutors say the actions Serhii K. is accused of — attacking civilian targets and causing explosions that destroyed infrastructure and damaged public services — would amount to a war crime. The alleged aim was to disrupt a major source of foreign revenue for Russia after its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, launched earlier that year. He is the only person on trial, but Croatian authorities have [USN:L6N44H0T9 TEXT:"arrested"] another man, identified as Vladimir Z., who prosecutors believe was one of the [USN:SPN44900E TEXT:"divers in the team"]. The explosion of Nord Stream sealed the end of Germany's longstanding dependence on Russian natural gas, although Moscow had already cut supplies over Berlin's support for European sanctions following Russia's February 2022 invasion of Ukraine. Germany previously received half its natural gas imports through the Nord Stream 1 pipeline, by far the biggest and most modern Russian pipeline serving western Europe, which allowed Russia to bypass Soviet-era pipelines transiting Ukraine. The supply had been due to double with the opening of a twin pipeline, Nord Stream 2, already built although Berlin cancelled approval to open it just prior to Russia's invasion of Ukraine. PLUMES OF METHANE GASE The trial, expected to continue into February next year, could also have domestic political implications. Germany's far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), leading in opinion polls for more than a year, has called for an end to military aid for Ukraine and a restoration of energy ties with Moscow. In the initial months after the pipelines were attacked, Western officials mainly pointed fingers at Russia. Moscow has always denied any involvement and called the suggestion it would blow up its own pipelines absurd. It also rejects charges that it has more recently targeted Western infrastructure with so-called "hybrid" sabotage and drone attacks. The Nord Stream system, lying at a depth of 80 to 110 metres under the Baltic and built by Russian gas concern Gazprom to supply up to 110 billion cubic metres of gas to Germany, was formerly at the core of economic ties between the two countries. On September 26, 2022, several blasts, some 17 hours apart, were detected by Swedish seismologists. The blasts sent huge plumes of methane gas into the atmosphere as three of the four concrete-coated steel pipelines were ruptured. Prosecutors allege that Serhii K. travelled to Germany through Poland some three weeks before the attack, using a forged Ukrainian passport. They say he and his group used a sailboat hired in the northern German city of Rostock to reach an area close to the Danish island of Bornholm, where they rigged specialised military-grade explosives fitted with timers to the sea floor. The weekly Der Spiegel magazine and ZDF public television have previously reported that five men and one woman were on the rented yacht Andromeda, which left Rostock on September 6 and returned on September 23, 2022.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro diz que não irá a debate da Band com Lula
item.description: O senador Flávio Bolsonaro, candidato do PL à Presidência, disse nesta terça-feira que não vai participar do debate presidencial da TV Band no próximo domingo, mas deixou aberta a possibilidade de participar do último debate a ser realizado antes do dia da votação em segundo turno, em 25 de outubro.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O senador Flávio Bolsonaro, candidato do PL à Presidência, disse nesta terça-feira que não vai participar do debate presidencial da TV Band no próximo domingo, mas deixou aberta a possibilidade de participar do último debate a ser realizado antes do dia da votação em segundo turno, em 25 de outubro. O debate da Band seria a primeira vez em que Flávio e o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva iriam contrapor, frente a frente, suas ideias. Nenhum dos dois participou de debates no primeiro turno. "Não vou, não está previsto esse debate domingo", disse, ao ser questionado se participaria do programa organizado pela Band que está marcado para as 20h do domingo. "Estamos analisando, quem vai dar a palavra final vai ser a minha equipe técnica de ir no último debate", afirmou, em entrevista após reunião em que recebeu apoio de parte do MDB. Logo nos primeiros dias após a realização do primeiro turno, Flávio anunciou sua [USN:L6N45S12O TEXT:"disposição"] de participar de debates. O senador venceu o primeiro turno com 47,03% dos votos válidos, contra 45,16% de Lula. Em texto publicado em seu site no início da noite desta terça-feira, a Band confirmou que o debate está mantido e que, segundo as regras estabelecidas pela emissora, "a ausência de qualquer um dos candidatos confirmados resultará na manutenção de um púlpito vazio no estúdio durante toda a transmissão". Pouco antes, Lula havia confirmado sua participação. "Domingo eu estarei no debate da Bandeirantes. Eu espero que o meu adversário compareça para que a gente possa fazer com que o povo tenha conhecimento da diferença de programa, da diferença de candidatura. Eu estarei lá", disse o presidente em um vídeo veiculado pela emissora em rede social. Lula havia optado por não participar de debates no primeiro turno, mas Flávio havia confirmado presença em um confronto que seria realizado pela TV Globo. O programa acabou cancelado em cima da hora, após a desistência do senador de participar. Lula já não participaria. E uma decisão da Justiça Eleitoral proibiu, pouco antes do horário do confronto, a exibição de púlpito vazio com o nome do petista. Adicionalmente, uma outra decisão determinou a participação do então candidato Renan Santos (Missão), um crítico de Flávio.

item.title: Supervisors at BHP's Escondida mine in Chile to strike after contract talks fail
item.description: The supervisors' union at BHP's Escondida copper mine in Chile said they will begin a strike on Wednesday after mediation efforts to tie up a new collective labor contract had failed, the union said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The supervisors' union at BHP's Escondida copper mine in Chile said they will begin a strike on Wednesday after mediation efforts to tie up a new collective labor contract had failed, the union said on Tuesday. The strike at the world's largest copper deposit threatens to tighten global supply and has been supporting copper prices. The union said it made a final offer incorporating 90% of company proposals plus key union demands including salary increases and production bonuses. BHP declined to respond and ended mediation talks, the union said in a statement late on Tuesday afternoon. The union said the company demanded workers give up essential benefits and insisted on sharing private biometric data with third parties. "The responsibility for this strike lies solely with the company and its negotiating committee," the union said in its statement. The supervisors' union and Escondida have been embroiled in [USN:L1N45M11Z TEXT:"fraught contract negotiations"] for several weeks, and had been threatening a strike if talks were to fail. The mine did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

item.title: Pedro Pascal says learning the cello for 'Behemoth!' was tougher than 'Game of Thrones' battle scenes
item.description: Hollywood star Pedro Pascal said learning to play the cello convincingly for Tony Gilroy's "Behemoth!" was the most challenging task of his career, joking he would rather relive one of his most brutal on-screen battles than learn how to play the instrument again.
item.dc:creator: Francesca Halliwell
item.content:encoded: Hollywood star Pedro Pascal said learning to play the cello convincingly for Tony Gilroy's "Behemoth!" was the most challenging task of his career, joking he would rather relive one of his most brutal on-screen battles than learn how to play the instrument again. Attending the movie's premiere at the London Film Festival on Tuesday, Pascal, who plays a talented cellist returning to Los Angeles after nearly two decades of touring, said the role left him more fearful than any previous project. "I'd never been so afraid," he said. "I've been nervous about other jobs and the physical...emotional demands, but it was nothing like this." Describing the challenge, the "Eddington" star joked: "I would choose fighting The Mountain in 'Game of Thrones' over learning how to play the cello convincingly. I would rather be, I don't know, tossed off of a cliff with Nicolas Cage than have to learn how to play the cello." Despite his fears, Pascal said working with the cello deepened his appreciation for an instrument he had long considered his favourite. "Once I held the cello, I felt good," he said. Seventeen-year-old "Thunderbolts*" star Alexa Swinton said working alongside Pascal showed her that success and kindness can go hand in hand, praising the actor's grace, poise and politeness on set. Beyond its family drama, "Behemoth!" aims to shine a light on the world of film scoring. Gilroy said that, prior to filming, even seasoned members of the crew had never stepped inside the scoring stages where much of the work takes place. The film's focus struck a chord with the musicians involved in the production. Actor Eva Victor recalled many telling the cast and crew: "Finally, a movie about us." The "Sorry, Baby" writer-director-actor said the film reveals a vital but frequently overlooked part of the movie-making process. "I think the curtain will be lifted on something that's really a huge part of film that we don't talk about or...we kind of take for granted often."

item.title: Trump administration to expand a Delek Texas refinery using Defense Production Act
item.description: The Trump administration will use the Cold War-era Defense Production Act to expand the processing capacity of a refinery in Texas owned by Delek US Holdings , Vice President JD Vance said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Trump administration will use the Cold War-era Defense Production Act to expand the processing capacity of a refinery in Texas owned by Delek US Holdings (DK.N) , Vice President JD Vance said on Tuesday. The Delek announcement is the latest in a series of White House moves aimed at taming fuel prices ahead of November's midterm elections, in which affordability has become a defining issue for voters. The push has included efforts to inject more diesel into the market — most controversially through a US general license easing restrictions on Russian-origin diesel, a step that drew criticism from Democrats and some Republicans alike. “Today I am pleased to announce that the Trump Administration, working with the refinery at Delek, has used the Defense Production Act and we’re going to expand the refinery right here in Tyler, Texas," Vance said while speaking in Texas. "We want millions of gallons of commercial grade and military-spec fuel to come out of this refinery in addition to what it's already producing," Vance said. "What that means for you and your families is lower cost to fly from one place to another, it means lower costs to drive your car into work every single day. It means a more reliable energy supply...," Vance said. The Tyler, Texas refinery, situated about 200 miles (322 km) north of Houston, currently processes about 74,000 barrels per day. The White House and Delek did not immediately respond to questions about how much funding is being allocated to the expansion or by how much it would increase refining capacity. Capacity [USN:L6N3Q20MK TEXT:"expansions at refineries"] typically are capital intensive and take many months, if not years, to complete depending on the complexity of the additions. Trump is expected in the coming days to issue a directive pushing administration officials to find ways to bypass state and local regulations blocking energy production and to use the Defense Production Act to expand refining capacity, Reuters reported last week.

item.title: Fóssil da Ilha de Wight lança luz sobre enigmáticos dinossauros carnívoros
item.description: O crânio parcial de um predador do tamanho de um tigre que vagava pelo que hoje é a Ilha de Wight, na costa sul da Inglaterra, há cerca de 120 milhões de anos, está proporcionando aos cientistas uma melhor compreensão de um grupo enigmático de dinossauros carnívoros, conhecidos por perseguir suas presas e despedaçá-las com garras enormes nas mãos.
item.dc:creator: Will Dunham
item.content:encoded: O crânio parcial de um predador do tamanho de um tigre que vagava pelo que hoje é a Ilha de Wight, na costa sul da Inglaterra, há cerca de 120 milhões de anos, está proporcionando aos cientistas uma melhor compreensão de um grupo enigmático de dinossauros carnívoros, conhecidos por perseguir suas presas e despedaçá-las com garras enormes nas mãos. Os pesquisadores afirmaram que o fóssil pertence a uma espécie que batizaram de Invictibellatrix amberina, um dos primeiros membros da linhagem de dinossauros carnívoros do Período Cretáceo conhecidos como megaraptoranos. O Invictibellatrix contribui para o conhecimento da anatomia craniana dos primeiros megaraptoranos e, por ser o primeiro espécime conhecido na Europa, ajuda a mostrar como o grupo se espalhou globalmente. O Invictibellatrix é um dos menores megaraptoranos. Com base em fósseis de megaraptoranos intimamente relacionados, os pesquisadores estimaram que o Invictibellatrix tinha cerca de 5 metros de comprimento, com o peso de um tigre grande. Seu corpo pode ter sido coberto por penas semelhantes a filamentos, afirmaram. Os megaraptoranos faziam parte do grupo chamado terópodes, que abrange todos os dinossauros carnívoros. “Os megaraptoranos são muito singulares entre os terópodes porque têm cabeças relativamente pequenas e delgadas, mas possuíam braços longos e fortes com garras enormes nas mãos, além de esqueletos de constituição muito leve”, disse Cassius Morrison, pesquisador de pós-doutorado da Universidade de Leeds, na Inglaterra, e autor principal do estudo publicado na revista Royal Society Open Science. “Essas características sugerem que os megaraptoranos eram caçadores ágeis, capazes de perseguir presas e usar seus braços grandes e garras para capturá-las e estripá-las com as garras das mãos”, disse Morrison. O maior megaraptorano conhecido, chamado Maip, tinha cerca de 10 metros de comprimento e habitava a Patagônia durante o crepúsculo da era dos dinossauros, cerca de 50 milhões de anos após a época em que o Invictibellatrix viveu. Megaraptoranos menores, como o Invictibellatrix, podem ter caçado presas menores, como mamíferos, répteis menores e filhotes de dinossauros. Os megaraptoranos maiores podem ter tido como alvo dinossauros herbívoros de maior porte, como os hadrossauros de bico de pato e os saurópodes de pescoço longo, embora provavelmente não os maiores deles. Os megaraptoranos caçavam de maneira oposta à de predadores gigantescos como o Tiranossauro rex. O Tiranossauro utilizava sua cabeça grande e robusta, dentes enormes e uma força de mordida incrível para matar presas, mas possuía braços fracos e de pouca utilidade na caça. O Invictibellatrix não era o principal predador da Ilha de Wight, já que havia terópodes maiores na região, além de vários dinossauros herbívoros, e pode ter desempenhado um papel semelhante ao da hiena atual. Há um debate entre os paleontólogos especializados em dinossauros sobre onde os megaraptoranos se encaixam na árvore genealógica dos terópodes. Apesar das diferenças em sua constituição física e na forma de caçar, uma hipótese é que os megaraptoranos eram intimamente relacionados aos tiranossauros, o grupo que incluía o Tiranossauro e outros que dominaram as paisagens da América do Norte e da Ásia no final do Cretáceo. O fóssil da Invictibellatrix, uma caixa craniana fragmentada, foi descoberto há cerca de um século e adquirido pelo Museu de História Natural de Londres em 1924. “Ele ficou guardado em uma das gavetas da coleção desde então, e ninguém o notou até alguns anos atrás”, disse Charlie Scherer, doutorando da University College London e coautor do estudo. Embora o Tiranossauro possa ser mais imponente que o Invictibellatrix, os pesquisadores observaram que, se uma pessoa fosse de alguma forma transportada de volta no tempo — como no recente filme “The End of Oak Street” —, o Invictibellatrix poderia representar um perigo maior. “Um terópode menor como o Invictibellatrix provavelmente teria sido uma ameaça muito maior para um ser humano do que algo como o T. rex, pois provavelmente seríamos pequenos demais para que o T. rex nos visse como uma refeição que valesse a pena, devido ao seu tamanho gigantesco e à quantidade de energia necessária para nos capturar”, disse Morrison. “Mas teríamos o tamanho perfeito para algo menor como o Invictibellatrix, já que pesamos cerca de um terço a um quarto do peso dele, o que nos tornaria uma refeição substancial e mais do que apenas um lanche. Além disso, o Invictibellatrix teria a agilidade e a manobrabilidade necessárias para perseguir e capturar um ser humano.”

item.title: Supervisores de mina chilena Escondida iniciarán huelga tras fracasar diálogo contractual
item.description: Los supervisores de la chilena Escondida, el mayor yacimiento mundial de cobre y controlado por BHP, iniciarán el miércoles una huelga tras el fracaso de una mediación que buscaba lograr un acuerdo para un nuevo contrato colectivo, dijo el martes el sindicato.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Los supervisores de la chilena Escondida, el mayor yacimiento mundial de cobre y controlado por BHP, iniciarán el miércoles una huelga tras el fracaso de una mediación que buscaba lograr un acuerdo para un nuevo contrato colectivo, dijo el martes el sindicato. El riesgo de una paralización en la mina ha estado apoyando los precios globales del metal en medio de los temores por una escasez de oferta. El sindicato dijo en un comunicado que no recibió una había realizado una propuesta en la víspera que esperaba que la empresa respondiera este jornada. "Minera Escondida decidió no responder y quebró las mesas de negociación, cerrando la Mediación Obligatoria sin acuerdo. Dado este escenario, la huelga del sindicato de supervisores y staff se hará efectiva mañana 14 de octubre a contar del primer turno de trabajo", detalló. Agregó que la empresa "exigió al sindicato renunciar a sus puntos y aceptar una propuesta deficiente que no contenía los puntos esenciales para nuestras bases". La propuesta mantenía pagos finales y préstamo blando por unos 30.000 dólares por socio. La empresa no respondió inmediatamente a una solicitud de comentarios. Sin embargo, en un boletín interno, Escondida confirmó que se iniciaría la paralización a las 8.00 local (1100 GMT) del miércoles pero acotó que la oferta mantenía su vigencia hasta la medianoche del martes y que "la dirigencia sindical tiene la facultad legal de aceptar la oferta hasta esa hora". Más temprano, el sindicato 1 de trabajadores emitió un boletín interno a sus socios donde los instó a suspender y abandonar sus labores en caso de que, a falta de supervisión, pudiera haber un riesgo inminente para su salud o vida.

item.title: Swisscom wins appeal in fibre-optic case, $21.6 million fine overturned
item.description: Swisscom said on Tuesday a court upheld its appeal against the Swiss competition watchdog's 2023 ruling that the telecom firm abused its market dominance in a fibre-optic case, overturning a fine of 18 million Swiss franc ($21.6 million).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Swisscom (SCMN.S) said on Tuesday a court upheld its appeal against the Swiss competition watchdog's 2023 ruling that the telecom firm abused its market dominance in a fibre-optic case, overturning a fine of 18 million Swiss franc ($21.6 million). The case relates to a probe opened by the Swiss Competition Commission in late 2020 into Swisscom's fibre-optic expansion on grounds it could exclude competitors and lead to the abuse of its leading market position The Federal Administrative Court ruled on Tuesday that Swisscom did not breach competition law and that the company does not hold a dominant position in the market as alleged by the competition watchdog Swisscom said it would review the judgment and assess implications for future network expansion The judgment is still subject to appeal before the federal court Swisscom's financial outlook for the 2026 financial year remains unchanged, the company said ($1 = 0.8327 Swiss francs)

item.title: Galderma agrees to buy ZO Skin Health for around $1.5 billion, sources say
item.description: Swiss skincare conglomerate Galderma has agreed to buy medical-grade skincare company ZO Skin Health for around $1.5 billion, according to two people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Abigail Summerville
item.content:encoded: Swiss skincare conglomerate Galderma (GALD.S) has agreed to buy medical-grade skincare company ZO Skin Health for around $1.5 billion, according to two people familiar with the matter. A deal could be announced in the coming days, the people said. ZO and Galderma, which were contacted outside regular business hours, did not immediately respond to requests for comment. ZO's owner, investment firm Blackstone (BX.N) , was exploring a sale of the company with investment banks Citigroup (C.N) and Raymond James (RJF.N) , Reuters [USN:L6N4500XQ TEXT:"reported"] last month. Blackstone declined to comment on Tuesday. The move by dermatology company Galderma, in which beauty giant L'Oréal (OREP.PA) owns a 20% stake, will expand its presence in the US market. In August, the company opened a US and Latin America headquarters in Miami. Established in 1981, Galderma also owns skincare brands Cetaphil and Alastin Skincare, Differin Epiduo acne gel, injectable neurotoxin Dysport, and dermal filler brand Restylane. Many strategic buyers are prioritizing clinically backed, physician-distributed skincare brands like ZO because of their efficacy and steadier demand versus over-the-counter products. Dermatologist Zein Obagi founded ZO in 2007. ZO sells skincare products including cleansers, serums, exfoliators and toners that are distributed by physicians and skincare professionals. Blackstone acquired ZO through its tactical opportunities fund in 2020.

item.title: Isle of Wight fossil sheds light on enigmatic meat-eating dinosaurs
item.description: The partial skull of a tiger-sized predator that prowled what is now the Isle of Wight off England's southern coast about 120 million years ago is giving scientists a better understanding of an enigmatic group of meat-eating dinosaurs known for running down prey and ripping them apart with massive hand claws.
item.dc:creator: Will Dunham
item.content:encoded: The partial skull of a tiger-sized predator that prowled what is now the [USN:L1N2XV167 TEXT:"Isle of Wight"] off England's southern coast about 120 million years ago is giving scientists a better understanding of an enigmatic group of [USN:L1N3U60NT TEXT:"meat-eating dinosaurs"] known for running down prey and ripping them apart with massive hand claws. Researchers said the fossil belongs to a species they have named Invictibellatrix amberina, an early member of the lineage of Cretaceous Period carnivorous dinosaurs called megaraptorans. Invictibellatrix adds to the knowledge of skull anatomy among early megaraptorans and, being the first one known from Europe, helps show how the group spread globally. Invictibellatrix is one of the smallest megaraptorans. Based on fossils of closely related megaraptorans, the researchers estimated that Invictibellatrix was about 16 feet (5 meters) long, with the weight of a large tiger. Its body may have been covered in filament-like feathers, they said. Megaraptorans were part of the group called theropods that spans all the meat-eating dinosaurs. "Megaraptorans are very unique among theropods because they have relatively small and slender heads but had long and strong arms with massive hand claws as well as very lightly built skeletons," said Cassius Morrison, a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Leeds in England and lead author of the study published in the journal Royal Society Open Science. "These characteristics imply that megaraptorans were agile hunters capable of chasing down prey and using their large arms and claws to catch them and disembowel them using their hand claws," Morrison said. The largest-known megaraptoran, named Maip, was about 33 feet (10 meters) long, inhabiting Patagonia during the twilight of the dinosaur age, about 50 million years after Invictibellatrix lived. Littler megaraptorans like Invictibellatrix may have hunted smaller prey like mammals, smaller reptiles and baby dinosaurs. Larger megaraptorans may have targeted bigger plant-eating dinosaurs like duckbilled hadrosaurs and long-necked sauropods, though probably not the biggest ones. Megaraptorans hunted in the opposite way from massive predators like [USN:L1N4560E4 TEXT:"Tyrannosaurus rex"]. Tyrannosaurus employed its large and stoutly built head, enormous teeth and incredible bite strength to kill prey, but had [USN:L1N41Y195 TEXT:"puny arms"] of little use in hunting. Invictibellatrix was not the Isle of Wight's top predator, with larger theropods around, alongside various herbivorous dinosaurs, and may have filled a role similar to a hyena today. There is a debate among dinosaur paleontologists as to where megaraptorans fit on the theropod family tree. Despite differences in how they were built and hunted, one hypothesis is that megaraptorans were closely related to tyrannosaurs, the group that included Tyrannosaurus and others that dominated the landscapes in North America and Asia later in the Cretaceous. 'UNCONQUERED FEMALE WARRIOR' Invictibellatrix means "unconquered female warrior." Morrison noted that after humble beginnings megaraptorans developed into apex predators in South America, Australia and Antarctica, becoming "the ruling queens," while the tyrannosaurs became the "tyrant kings" in North America and Asia. Scientists are trying to unravel the evolutionary history of megaraptorans. A leading hypothesis has megaraptorans originating in Asia before migrating through Europe into Africa and then on into South America, thriving until the dinosaurs were doomed by an asteroid strike 66 million years ago. This hypothesis was lacking fossil evidence because no megaraptorans had been known from Europe until now. "These findings help to uncover the evolution of one of the most mysterious theropod groups," University College London doctoral student and study co-author Charlie Scherer said. The Invictibellatrix fossil, a fragmented braincase, was discovered about a century ago and acquired by the Natural History Museum in London in 1924. "It was left in one of the collection's drawers ever since, and no one noticed it until a couple of years ago," Scherer said. While Tyrannosaurus may be more imposing than Invictibellatrix, the researchers noted that if a person were somehow transported back in time — like in the recent film "The End of Oak Street" — Invictibellatrix might present more of a danger. "A smaller theropod like Invictibellatrix would likely have been a much bigger threat to a human than something like T. rex because we would likely be too small for T. rex to see as a worthwhile meal because of how massive it was and the amount of energy it would be required to catch us," Morrison said. "But we would be the perfect size for something smaller like Invictibellatrix, as we are about a third to a quarter of its weight, making us a good hearty meal and more than just a snack. Additionally, Invictibellatrix would have the agility and maneuverability to pursue and catch a human."

item.title: Torrential rains in Libya's Tripoli kill two
item.description: Torrential downpours flooded the Libyan capital of Tripoli on Tuesday, killing two people, according to a statement by authorities and a local TV channel.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Torrential downpours flooded the Libyan capital of Tripoli on Tuesday, killing two people, according to a statement by authorities and a local TV channel. Jumhouria Bank said an employee died due to an electrical shock. The Tripoli Red Crescent said in a statement it recovered the man's body during the flooding. Rescue teams recovered the body of another man from his car, which was submerged in the floodwaters, according to a local TV station. Fadel Abu Arqoub, the mayor of Central Tripoli, told the TV station that the rain lasted for 2-1/2 hours and that the situation was catastrophic. The state-owned electricity company said it cut off power as a precaution in certain areas where rising water reached homes. Eyewitnesses said the floodwaters inundated roads and submerged numerous vehicles.

item.title: Big UK firms focus on cost-cutting as inflation bites, Deloitte survey shows
item.description: Large British companies expect inflation and interest rates to rise over the next year and are focussing increasingly on cost-cutting, a survey published Deloitte showed on Wednesday, two weeks before finance minister John Healey's first budget.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Large British companies expect inflation and interest rates to rise over the next year and are focussing increasingly on cost-cutting, a survey published Deloitte showed on Wednesday, two weeks before finance minister John Healey's first budget. Here are key findings from the quarterly survey of chief financial officers (CFOs) by Deloitte which gauges the mood across British boardrooms and is watched by the government and Bank of England. • CFOs expect inflation to be 3.4% in a year's time, up from 3.0% in the previous quarter's survey • They expect the Bank of England's key interest rate to be 4.0% in a year from now, above its current level of 3.75% • Deloitte said the proportion of CFOs who described credit as costly hit a two-and-a-half-year high • "A decade of leadership turnovers, growing political fragmentation and near-constant speculation on tax policy has clouded the backdrop for business," said Debapratim De, chief economist at Deloitte UK • 68% of CFOs rated cost reduction as a strong priority for the next 12 months, up from 53% in the previous survey • CFOs ranked the prospect of further rate rises in Britain and the United States as the second-biggest risk to their businesses, with a score of 65%, up from 59% • Geopolitics stayed top at 67% • The survey of 66 CFOs, including those of 12 FTSE 100 and 25 FTSE 250 companies, was conducted between September 17 and October 1

item.title: African financial markets gain ground but liquidity a challenge, survey shows
item.description: African countries are making steady progress in building financial markets that can help businesses raise money and fund infrastructure, but thin trading remains a hurdle to attracting investment and financing growth, an annual survey showed.
item.dc:creator: Colleen Goko
item.content:encoded: African countries are making steady progress in building financial markets that can help businesses raise money and fund infrastructure, but thin trading remains a hurdle to attracting investment and financing growth, an annual survey showed. The 2026 Africa Financial Markets Index, compiled by Absa bank and think tank OMFIF, found that 21 of the 29 countries surveyed recorded higher scores as easing inflation, stronger foreign exchange reserves and regulatory reforms helped deepen markets. The gains come against a backdrop of rising trade tensions, conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East and elevated energy costs, which the report warned could undermine economic stability across the continent. "The global environment is far from straightforward," Absa Group Chief Executive Kenny Fihla wrote in the report, pointing to risks including a super [USN:L1N45U0J2 TEXT:"El Nino"]. "In these complex times, all countries must bolster their fundamentals to best weather the storm. Happily, many African countries are in that very position," he said. South Africa retained the top spot, followed by Mauritius and Namibia. Cape Verde was the biggest mover, climbing six places to 13th on stronger foreign exchange reserves and new sustainable finance initiatives. Ghana rose four places to sixth as falling inflation, stronger stock market activity and improving economic conditions aided its recovery from a debt crisis. Botswana and Nigeria each slipped two places to seventh and eighth respectively. Nigeria was hurt by weaker foreign exchange access and transparency scores, while Botswana suffered from [USN:L1N44O0EW TEXT:"rising inflation"]. The index measures how easily countries can raise and move capital, examining stock and bond markets, access to foreign currency, pension savings, economic conditions and regulation. Developing these markets can help businesses access financing beyond traditional bank loans and channel savings into infrastructure and other long-term investments. But the report found that expanding financial products and market infrastructure had not consistently translated into greater trading activity, leaving liquidity an ongoing challenge. African markets are seeking to support larger fundraising efforts, including billionaire Aliko Dangote's ongoing [USN:L8N45Y14M TEXT:"refinery IPO"] in Nigeria, which is aiming to raise billions of dollars from retail and institutional investors. Now in its 10th year, the index introduced a revised methodology measuring countries against fixed benchmarks of good practice rather than against one another. Historical scores were recalculated to allow comparisons. The average score reached 56, its highest in a decade.

item.title: SoftBank junk bond sale raises stakes for CEO Son's all-in AI bet
item.description: SoftBank's promise to pay its highest-ever yields in a record $11 billion junk-bond offering highlights the pressure on CEO Masayoshi Son to secure returns on his all-in bet on AI amid concerns about possible overheating in the market.
item.dc:creator: Anton Bridge
item.content:encoded: SoftBank's (9984.T) promise to pay its highest-ever yields in a record $11 billion junk-bond offering highlights the pressure on CEO Masayoshi Son to secure returns on his all-in bet on AI amid concerns about possible overheating in the market. The SoftBank debt issuance last month added to a sharp surge in corporate borrowing this year, including major bond sales from Amazon.com (AMZN.O) , Alphabet (GOOGL.O) and [USN:L1N45Z00N TEXT:"Tencent"] (0700.HK) . The scale of Son's investments, which include backing totalling $64.6 billion for ChatGPT maker OpenAI, in particular, has made the technology-and-investing conglomerate a bellwether for AI sentiment. Those fresh investments are now coming under sharper scrutiny by analysts and investors amid worries about the degree of concentration in SoftBank's portfolio and whether a payoff from the expenditures by AI companies will come soon enough. SoftBank previously sold shares in Nvidia (NVDA.O) and T-Mobile US (TMUS.O) to fund its investments, but it is now borrowing at record yields of up to 9.75% in order to retain assets that it believes will appreciate, a senior SoftBank executive told Reuters. "We've borrowed money in large part because we don't want to sell assets that we believe will keep rising in value," said Alex Clavel, CEO of SoftBank Investment Advisers, which manages the Vision Funds. Sam Altman's OpenAI is the core investment in the latest iteration of Son's investment strategy, following lucrative bets on Chinese tech giant Alibaba (9988.HK) and chip designer Arm . “Given OpenAI’s appreciation to date, 9.75% is still very reasonable," Clavel said. Arm's valuation has grown fivefold since it floated in 2023 and further listings from SoftBank's private AI portfolio would clarify their value and more easily allow the assets to be monetised for additional investment activity. Altman has said OpenAI will not go public this year, citing safety concerns about AI. It also faces competition from rival Anthropic and hyperscalers, as well as low-cost Chinese labs. SoftBank was previously "betting on a bunch of numbers at the roulette table. Now it's red or black, either lose everything or gain everything," MST Financial analyst David Gibson said. INCREASED SCRUTINY OF AI-RELATED FUNDRAISING SoftBank will pay its highest-ever coupon of 9.75% on a bond issued last month that matures in 2034. That return compares with Alphabet (GOOGL.O) offering 5.2% for a bond issued in August that matures in 2033. SoftBank's shares surged to a record high of 8,632 yen in June, though they have fallen 38% since then, while its credit default swap spreads - the cost to insure its debt against a default or other credit event - jumped 24% over the same period. SoftBank's higher yields reflect investor perceptions of their risk and concentration in large positions, analysts say. "The bets are much bigger than we've ever seen," said Amir Anvarzadeh of Asymmetric Advisors, who recommends shorting the stock. James Athey, a fixed-income portfolio manager at Marlborough, said the fund was not allocating to high-yield bonds at this stage of the credit cycle, given current tight spread levels. "SoftBank is so aggressive, so concentrated and so all-in, I don't think we'd be looking there first anyway," he said. Clavel, however, says SoftBank's OpenAI backing reflects their deep business ties. "We see OpenAI as a partner, building a relationship that can deliver strategic value as well as financial returns," he said. OpenAI is also an investor in and customer of data centre company SB Energy (SBE.O) , which SoftBank is looking to list and may seek a valuation of $50 billion, Reuters has reported. "SoftBank is taking advantage of hyper-excitement around AI-driven businesses, applying very high valuations for relatively low revenues, and they are looking to capitalize," said MST's Gibson of the potential valuation. Son's bets have a mixed track record - his investment in Chinese tech giant Alibaba (9988.HK) was a major success, but Son also directed $16 billion to Adam Neumann's WeWork, which ultimately went bankrupt. Other setbacks included a crash in the value of its investments as central banks moved to hike rates in 2022. "OpenAI's value appreciation to date far exceeds the losses in our 2021 vintage investments," Clavel said. Over the decades, Son has navigated market peaks and troughs to build SoftBank into a 30 trillion yen ($189.9 billion) company. "Being priced in is a massive transformation of the workplace with AI effectively taking over a big chunk of what gets done with human brains now," said Morningstar senior equity analyst Dan Baker. "If that goes ahead it's hard to see their investments not being very successful," he said.

item.title: El Salvador's Bukele says Spain's Cox Energy to invest $2.9 billion
item.description: Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele on Tuesday announced a $2.9 billion investment by Spanish firm Cox Energy to develop energy, water, and fuel projects in the country.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele on Tuesday announced a $2.9 billion investment by Spanish firm Cox Energy to develop energy, water, and fuel projects in the country. The package includes a $1.8 billion natural gas storage plant that would enable energy sales to other countries, along with solar energy, water and sanitation components. $600 million for water and sanitation improvements. $300 million for solar energy storage batteries, with a capacity of 440 megawatts and potential to expand to 1 gigawatt. $200 million will be invested to develop a photovoltaic plant. "This will directly benefit Salvadoran families," Bukele told reporters, adding that the benefits would materialize once a new power plant to be built by Cox becomes operational.

item.title: Advogado de diretora do Fed questiona mais recente tentativa de Trump de destituí-la
item.description: O advogado da diretora do Federal Reserve Lisa Cook questionou a objetividade de uma investigação da Casa Branca sobre as alegações de que ela teria cometido fraude hipotecária, de acordo com uma carta à qual a Reuters teve acesso nesta terça-feira, contestando a mais recente tentativa do presidente Donald Trump de destituí-la do cargo.
item.dc:creator: Ann Saphir
item.content:encoded: O advogado da diretora do Federal Reserve Lisa Cook questionou a objetividade de uma investigação da Casa Branca sobre as alegações de que ela teria cometido fraude hipotecária, de acordo com uma carta à qual a Reuters teve acesso nesta terça-feira, contestando a mais recente tentativa do presidente Donald Trump de destituí-la do cargo. Trump vem tentando demitir Cook há mais de um ano, à medida que busca exercer maior controle sobre um banco central que, segundo ele, se recusa, por motivos políticos, a reduzir as taxas de juros. Cook nega qualquer irregularidade e entrou com uma ação judicial para manter seu cargo. Na semana passada, Trump anunciou uma nova investigação sobre Cook e a nomeação de uma comissão de três pessoas para conduzir uma audiência. Posteriormente, o presidente disse a repórteres que seguiria adiante com a demissão dela caso a comissão recomendasse isso. Os advogados de Cook afirmaram que uma audiência justa demonstraria que não há base legal para demiti-la. Na carta desta terça-feira, o advogado de Cook, Abbe Lowell, observou que um dos membros propostos para a comissão, o assessor de política econômica da Casa Branca, Kevin Hassett, já havia pressionado Cook a se afastar do cargo e sugerido que Trump tinha “motivo” para demiti-la. “Uma audiência com membros comprovadamente tendenciosos, alegações adicionais não especificadas e um cronograma pouco claro para a divulgação de quaisquer provas adicionais – sem nenhuma explicação sobre por que elas não foram apresentadas anteriormente – não é um processo que respeite a aparência ou o histórico de independência”, escreveu Lowell. Lowell afirmou que Cook não poderia comparecer a uma audiência na data de 5 de novembro anunciada pela Casa Branca, pois estaria cumprindo suas funções na Europa “em reuniões de política financeira e monetária”. O mais cedo que Cook poderia comparecer a qualquer audiência seria após a reunião de política monetária do Fed marcada para 8 e 9 de dezembro, escreveu ele. Uma decisão da Suprema Corte no caso de Cook, mais cedo neste ano, impediu Trump de demitir um diretor do Fed à vontade, ressaltando a necessidade de o Fed permanecer politicamente independente tanto na prática quanto na aparência para poder desempenhar suas funções. Mas a decisão também abriu caminho para uma possível destituição, caso seja dada a uma autoridade do Fed a oportunidade justa de examinar as provas das alegações e a chance de refutá-las. A Casa Branca parece estar buscando esse caminho. O Fed elevou sua taxa básica de juros em setembro e deve fazê-lo novamente em sua última reunião do ano.

item.title: Engenheiro da OpenAI é preso por instalar dispositivo de espionagem na empresa, dizem EUA
item.description: Policiais federais dos Estados Unidos prenderam um cidadão saudita que era engenheiro na OpenAI e é suspeito de instalar um dispositivo oculto de gravação de áudio em uma sala de reuniões executiva da empresa de inteligência artificial, informou o Departamento de Justiça do país nesta terça-feira.
item.dc:creator: Jaspreet Singh
item.content:encoded: Policiais federais dos Estados Unidos prenderam um cidadão saudita que era engenheiro na OpenAI e é suspeito de instalar um dispositivo oculto de gravação de áudio em uma sala de reuniões executiva da empresa de inteligência artificial, informou o Departamento de Justiça do país nesta terça-feira. Abdulrahman Alfozan, de 35 anos, era engenheiro na OpenAI desde julho de 2025, informou o Departamento de Justiça em comunicado. A OpenAI descobriu o dispositivo conectado a uma porta USB na parte traseira de um televisor em uma sala de conferências executiva em um de seus prédios em São Francisco em 30 de setembro, segundo o departamento. O dispositivo tem o tamanho de um polegar, possui um microfone e pode ser conectado a uma câmera. O aparelho estava escondido em papel higiênico, de acordo com a denúncia do FBI. Ele foi instalado por volta de 28 de setembro e os dados armazenados estão criptografados e inacessíveis. Posteriormente, os investigadores encontraram um dispositivo personalizado semelhante na bolsa pessoal de Alfozan. A OpenAI afirmou na rede social X que utilizou seus modelos internos de IA para identificar a pessoa responsável por instalar o dispositivo e rastrear sua origem. A empresa afirmou ter evidências de que o funcionário pretendia colocar outros dispositivos de gravação em áreas sensíveis de seus escritórios para gravar reuniões secretamente. “No momento, não temos indícios de que esse indivíduo tenha acessado indevidamente ou extraído modelos, código-fonte ou dados de clientes. O funcionário foi demitido”, afirmou a empresa. A OpenAI encaminhou o caso ao FBI, que continua investigando. A embaixada da Arábia Saudita nos EUA não respondeu imediatamente a um pedido feito pela Reuters para comentário. “Abdulrahman Alfozan teria escondido um dispositivo de gravação secreto dentro da sala de conferências executiva de seu empregador para capturar secretamente comunicações confidenciais sobre a tecnologia de superinteligência da empresa”, afirmou o diretor da polícia federal dos EUA (FBI), Kash Patel, em comunicado. Alfozan também teria utilizado um agente de produtividade baseado em IA para buscar informações sobre agendas e capacidades das salas de reuniões por cerca de um mês, até 16 de setembro, de acordo com a denúncia do FBI. Ele é residente permanente legal nos EUA desde setembro de 2020. Se condenado, Alfozan pode pegar até cinco anos de prisão, multa de US$250 mil e três anos de liberdade condicional. Alfozan estudou no Instituto de Tecnologia de Massachusetts (MIT) e na Universidade da Califórnia, em Berkeley, de acordo com seu perfil no LinkedIn. Anteriormente, ele trabalhou na Meta e na Microsoft. A Reuters não conseguiu verificar de forma independente os detalhes mencionados em seu perfil no LinkedIn. A OpenAI informou na sexta-feira que demitiu três pesquisadores após uma investigação ter constatado que eles haviam violado políticas da empresa sobre o tratamento de informações confidenciais. Os pesquisadores, Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak e Mikita Balesni, publicaram posteriormente uma carta detalhando as circunstâncias de sua demissão e argumentando que cortes em massa abruptos podem criar incerteza entre os funcionários e minar uma cultura na qual os pesquisadores podem levantar questões de segurança.

item.title: Martinez slams Man Utd hierarchy after Atletico defeat
item.description: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez criticised the club's hierarchy after their 2-0 Champions League defeat by Atletico Madrid on Tuesday, saying he expected greater investment to help the team compete at the highest level.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez criticised the club's hierarchy after their 2-0 Champions League defeat by Atletico Madrid on Tuesday, saying he expected greater investment to help the team compete at the highest level. The Argentina international singled out director of football Jason Wilcox, saying United needed more signings to compete with their rivals and build a squad capable of challenging in Europe. "I expect more from our technical director. I have to be honest. And also, as players, we have to do more," Martinez told Amazon Prime. Atletico took the lead through Pablo Barrios inside the opening minute at the Metropolitano, before Ademola Lookman sealed the victory in the 79th minute, shortly after United defender Leny Yoro was sent off. The result stretched Michael Carrick’s side’s winless run to five matches in all competitions and left them on three points in the Champions League league phase, having opened their campaign with a 4-0 win over Sabah FK. United are returning to the [USN:L6N45Z15P TEXT:"Champions League"] after a two-season absence, having finished bottom of their group in their previous appearance in the competition in 2023-24. "We had a fantastic season last season and now we expect more from the top, from upstairs, to bring in more players to compete, because many teams have brought in many players as well," Martinez said. United, who sit 13th in the Premier League, visit Leeds United on Sunday before travelling to Como for their next Champions League fixture on October 21.

item.title: LSU coach Will Wade won’t fight SEC on RJ Luis eligibility
item.description: If anything is certain about LSU's men's basketball roster three weeks before the season, it's that RJ Luis won't be part of it.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: If anything is certain about LSU's men's basketball roster three weeks before the season, it's that RJ Luis won't be part of it. Coach Will Wade said Tuesday that the Tigers won't fight the SEC over Luis's eligibility, who has signed multiple professional contracts since his last college appearance. "We're going to follow all the SEC protocols with him," Wade said. "I think it's been pretty clear what the SEC protocols are around that. He didn't travel with us to McNeese (for a recent exhibition game), and he hasn't been rostered." Wade was referring to a rule the conference passed earlier this year that outlaws rostering players who have spent any time with a professional team from returning to college basketball or football at an SEC member institution. Luis, a former Big East Player of the Year with St. John's, went undrafted in 2025, signed a two-way contract with the Utah Jazz and was soon traded to the Boston Celtics. Luis was waived by Boston but signed an Exhibit 10 contract with the Celtics before being released again. He subsequently joined the G League's Maine Celtics but never appeared in a regular-season game. Luis attempted to return to college when he committed to LSU in May. But he was not part of the Tigers' roster earlier this month when they played McNeese, one of Wade's former schools, in an exhibition. LSU had just 10 players available, although only seven appeared in the game. The Tigers' revamped roster in Wade's first season includes guards Donovan Dent and Skyy Clark, both of whom have received a fifth season of eligibility via a California court case. They also hope to have Senegalese-Italian forward Saliou Niang, selected 58th in the 2025 NBA Draft, and French center Brice Dessert, who went undrafted. But their eligibility is in doubt because of a new SEC regulation banning players who did not "properly" withdraw from the NBA draft before attempting to return to college. Wade didn't have much clarity to offer, three weeks before the Tigers are scheduled to open the season against LSU New Orleans. "We'll see. We'll see who gets eligible," Wade said. "We feel good about that group getting eligible -- the ones who were actually on our roster, the ones who are actually on our team. We feel like those guys will get eligible." --Field Level Media

item.title: LPGA commish calls Good Good Callaway driver ad fallout ‘brutal’
item.description: LPGA commissioner Craig Kessler called the controversy surrounding Good Good Golf's Callaway ad "brutal" and "heartbreaking," while arguing that people should have a chance to learn from serious mistakes.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: LPGA commissioner Craig Kessler called the controversy surrounding Good Good Golf's Callaway ad "brutal" and "heartbreaking," while arguing that people should have a chance to learn from serious mistakes. Kessler addressed the August advertisement Tuesday at the Front Office Sports Tuned In summit. The video promoting a co-branded Callaway driver showed Good Good co-founder Garrett Clark shoving fellow content creator Alexis Miestowski to the ground after she reached for the club. The spot drew widespread criticism over its depiction of violence against women and was quickly removed. Good Good claimed the spot was intended as a parody of the horror movie "Obsession." "The fact that someone thought that was a good idea, and it came to life, just shows you that while society has made enormous progress, we have a very, very long way to go," Kessler said. Callaway ended its relationship with Good Good and pledged $1 million to organizations working to prevent violence against women. Good Good also withdrew as title sponsor of a PGA Tour event, while retailers pulled its merchandise and Golf Channel canceled the 2026 season of its reality competition series "Big Break x Good Good." The LPGA did not have a partnership with Good Good. Kessler acknowledged the criticism but argued that people should have opportunities to admit mistakes and learn from them. "Good people make mistakes, and we have to leave room in society for someone to say, ‘I made a massive mistake. Please forgive me. Here's what I learned, and it won't happen again,'" Kessler said. Kessler drew a parallel to criticism he received earlier this year after canceling the final round of the LPGA's season opener because of cold weather, a decision for which he later apologized. "Brutal that it happened -- awful -- my heart goes out to anybody who was affected, and I think a lot of lessons were learned," Kessler said of the Good Good controversy. --Field Level Media

item.title: Dodgers' dynasty on the ropes as bats go cold against Brewers
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers have spent the last two Octobers spraying champagne. This year they may be facing an early winter.
item.dc:creator: Rory Carroll
item.content:encoded: The Los Angeles Dodgers have spent the last two Octobers spraying champagne. This year they may be facing an early winter. The two-time defending World Series champions trail the Milwaukee Brewers 2-0 in the National League Championship Series after a 7-4 loss on Monday. Their pitching has wobbled and their lineup has barely made a sound. On Monday, Milwaukee shattered Yoshinobu Yamamoto's aura of postseason invincibility. Christian Yelich hit a two-run single to knock out the 2025 World Series MVP after just 2-2/3 innings. A day earlier, the Brewers chased prized midseason acquisition Tarik Skubal after five innings on their way to a 2-1 win in Game One. Still, the mound is not the Dodgers' biggest problem. Their star-studded lineup is hitting .193 this postseason and is 2-for-26 with runners in scoring position. On Monday they managed three hits. Shohei Ohtani’s bat has also gone quiet. The four-time MVP has been playing through problems with his left knee, right biceps and neck, and it shows. He went 0-for-4 with two strikeouts on Monday. He is now batting .150 (3-for-20) in the postseason, with seven strikeouts and no extra-base hits. The slump is bad enough that Dodgers manager Dave Roberts is reportedly considering what once seemed unthinkable: benching Ohtani for Game Three in Los Angeles on Wednesday. Rookie Josue De Paula would likely replace him at designated hitter. "Obviously it hasn't been good," Roberts told The Athletic after the loss. "He doesn't feel great. I think for me, it's having a conversation with him tomorrow, kind of try to figure out what's best for him, what's best for us." The Dodgers have escaped tight spots before. In last year's Fall Classic, they trailed the Toronto Blue Jays 3-2 and won the last two games to take the title. Shortstop Mookie Betts had a simple answer. "We just have to figure out a way to get hits," he said. "That's really it. There's no magic to it."

item.title: GameStop CEO Cohen buys shares worth nearly $23 million

Here are more details: Cohen bought 844,130 shares between $26.75 and $27 apiece, increasing his stake to 46.2 million shares This marks Cohen's [USN:L6N45O14A TEXT:"second purchase"] of GameStop stock this month. He bought $17.1 million worth of shares, according to an SEC filing on October 2 Analysts generally view insider purchases as a sign that executives are confident in a company's prospects and believe its shares are undervalued Earlier this year, GameStop sought to acquire eBay, roughly four times its market value, for about $56 billion. EBay [USN:L4N4470RD TEXT:"rejected"] the offer as "neither credible nor attractive" In August, Bloomberg news reported that Cohen was [USN:L4N4470RD TEXT:"considering"] abandoning his pursuit of eBay and instead pursuing a partnership or joint venture with the ecommerce major GameStop's shares have risen 35.6% so far this year

item.title: US top diplomat Marco Rubio to visit India and Uzbekistan
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio will depart on Saturday on a five-day trip to India and Uzbekistan, the State Department said, adding that he will discuss energy cooperation in India.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh, Simon Lewis
item.content:encoded: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio will depart on Saturday on a five-day trip to India and Uzbekistan, the State Department said, adding that he will discuss energy cooperation in India. Rubio will travel to Samarkand in Uzbekistan and to Mumbai and Jamnagar in India, the State Department said in a statement on Tuesday. In India, Rubio will meet government officials to "exchange views on regional and global dynamics, and discuss prospects for enhanced energy cooperation," the statement said. Indian and American officials [USN:L1N45S0MJ TEXT:"indicated earlier this month"] that long-running efforts to finalize a bilateral trade agreement have stalled again. US-India ties [USN:L4N45S0BG TEXT:"have been rocky this past year"] over issues including President Donald Trump's repeated claim of brokering an India-Pakistan ceasefire and a [USN:SPN42H00F TEXT:"US military attack"] on a ship off Oman that killed three Indian seafarers. New Delhi has also [USN:L1N45G03K TEXT:"raised concerns"] over US legislation allowing Trump to impose tariffs of up to 100% on countries that purchase Russian energy, part of Washington's efforts to pressure Moscow over its invasion of Ukraine. India only briefly reduced purchases from Russia in early 2026 but they have since jumped, especially since the supply shock that followed the US-Israeli war on Iran . The announcement of Rubio's visit also comes during ongoing protests in India [USN:L4N45Z0IJ TEXT:"over the removal of 130 million voters"] from electoral rolls. Washington has thus far not commented on the demonstrations. In Uzbekistan, Rubio will participate in bilateral engagements with officials from Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Kyrgyzstan, and lead a delegation of over 200 business leaders, the State Department said.

item.title: Japanese PM’s reflationist label is hard to shake
item.description: Sanae Takaichi dislikes the depiction of her year-old administration. But a $2 trln investment splurge and profligate budget are more apt to stoke inflation. Mooted tax cuts push up bond yields while her central bank choices weaken the yen. The biggest risk is that she succeeds.
item.dc:creator: Hudson Lockett
item.content:encoded: Sanae Takaichi chafes at the word "reflationist". Top officials in the Japanese prime minister's administration [USN:P8N3KU036 TEXT:"argue her policies"], which include a $2.3 trillion investment splurge and looser budgeting processes, will not intensify the inflation she vowed to tame on the campaign trail. They're probably wrong: the biggest risk to Japan's economy is that she succeeds. Since the country's first female leader [USN:L6N3VN03G TEXT:"took charge"] 12 months ago it has become clear that her policy program, dubbed “Takaichinomics”, is based on a misunderstanding of what drives Japan's growth. As she readies to pass her first national budget since an [USN:L6N3Z502S TEXT:"electoral landslide"] in February, this mistake threatens not only to further lift prices but also to undermine the virtuous economic cycle which has delivered the Asian country from decades in the doldrums. Bond and currency markets have been rattled repeatedly by Takaichi’s attempts to shrug off the structural limitations imposed on her recent predecessors by Japan's looming debt and graying workforce. But where the late Prime Minister Shinzo Abe used monetary and fiscal stimulus to rouse the economy from a deflationary stupor, the current incumbent wants sharply higher spending to turbo-charge growth at a time when prices are already rising. To her credit, there are signs she is partially changing course. After a year of [USN:L6N42O0IO TEXT:"tacitly pressuring"] the Bank of Japan to slow-roll rate rises in order to keep government funding costs down, Takaichi is now attempting to [USN:L4N45S0EK TEXT:"shed her reputation"] as a monetary reflationist. The shift is in part due to the sliding yen, combined with a government bond selloff that has pushed up yields and invited [USN:L6N45A09Y TEXT:"public pressure"] from US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. Ayano Sato, one of two central bank board appointees who unnerved markets by voting against last month’s hike, even [USN:L4N45S1J9 TEXT:"voiced tepid support"] for more rate rises in a recent Reuters interview. That’s potentially positive for the Japanese currency, which has weakened about 7% against the dollar since Takaichi took charge of the Liberal Democratic Party. Yet the prime minister still [USN:SPN45900X TEXT:"refuses to fully explain"] how she plans to cover the revenue shortfall from scrapping food taxes for at least two years — her flagship measure for providing inflationary relief to households. This is one reason why yields on 30-year Japanese government bonds recently hit a record high of more than 4.2%. Official reassurances that fiscal policy will be both “responsible and proactive” have failed to assuage investors worried by the implications of sharply higher spending for sovereign debt, which is near 200% of GDP. The 65-year-old believes large-scale government-led investment is the only prescription for the economic malady of lacklustre growth she diagnosed in February, after her party regained control of the legislature’s powerful lower house. However, while the contribution to growth from increases in the capital stock may be lower than in the 1980s boom, average annual investment over the past decade still clocks in at 25% of Japanese GDP, per Capital Economics, the highest level among the Group of Seven rich economies. Additional government investment is more likely to intensify inflation. Previous administrations focused instead on improving labour mobility and bringing in overseas workers to offset Japan’s shrinking population. These efforts helped free up more productive workers to seek better-paying jobs, while also providing [USN:L6N4340H3 TEXT:"enough ready hands"] for private investment projects. The upshot has been a return of wage-driven inflation which, though disquieting for households used to stable prices, helped spur Japan’s economic revival. By contrast, Takaichi has thrown up new barriers to long-term residency for imported labour while delaying her predecessor’s plans to raise Japan's minimum wage. In July she downplayed the role of inflation in driving growth in her first economic policy blueprint , blaming “chronically insufficient investment in the future” for kneecapping potential GDP. Her proposed solution envisages a 370 trillion yen ($2.3 trillion) public-private investment plan to [USN:L6N45205U TEXT:"more than double GDP growth"] by 2040, as well as removing limits on annual budget requests by government ministries. Their latest submissions imply spending will jump by 14% to a [USN:L4N44V0T2 TEXT:"record 143 trillion yen"] for the 2027 fiscal year. The sharp increase is supposed to partly reflect outlays previously left to supplementary budgets, which Takaichi wants to scrap. But emergency spending packages may endure given their utility for voter-pleasing initiatives, such as the June move to [USN:L4N42A1YD TEXT:"subsidise fuel costs"]. Rising interest rates further complicate the picture. Increased borrowing costs not only raise the burden of funding the government but also servicing its existing debt, which is set to reach about 37 trillion yen next year. Ayako Fujita, Japan chief economist at JPMorgan, estimates the bond issuance necessary to cover both the prime minister's budget plans and interest payments will likely lead to an increase in Japan’s debt-to-GDP ratio during the 2027 fiscal year, ending four straight years of decline. That risks triggering a vicious cycle as investors dump longer-dated government bonds and push yields still higher. The bank estimates this could help push the closely watched ratio back above 200% by 2031. Supporters of the prime minister’s policies shrug off inflation concerns and argue higher growth will expand the tax base to offset any revenue lost from tax cuts, while returns on government-led investments will help cover further outlays. Yet new plans to [USN:L4N45U03W TEXT:"reboot"] Japan's version of the [USN:L6N3WX0YY TEXT:"now-defunct"] US Department of Government Efficiency in order to scrounge for unused government funds suggest mounting pressure to cover spending. And as countries like China have [USN:L4N43V09D TEXT:"learned the hard way"], the investment success rate for state-backed projects is low. A massive injection of government funding into Japan’s financial system may instead crowd out private investment as the shrinking labour force creates a bottleneck for viable projects. That could prompt domestic investors to seek returns overseas, undermining Tokyo’s efforts to repatriate capital and increasing downward pressure on the yen. Far from delivering a growth boost, Takaichi’s investment drive looks more likely to distort markets and undermine the factors behind Japan’s recent economic renaissance. The best-case scenario is for the prime minister’s audacious plan to either fail or be diverted. Otherwise she may attract far worse labels than "reflationist".
